Minor differences from the paper's Table 3 rendering, where the label was kept: E2 'Non-face-to-face-communication' (Table 3: 'Non-face-to-face communication'); E17 'Ability to work from home – I know...' (Table 3 has no spaces around the dash; Discussion paraphrases as 'Having the ability to work from home'). There is no E4/Enjoy_04 anywhere in the file (the raw multi-select string column 'Emjoy' never contains 4) and the paper states 23 options, so the gap is the study's own numbering. instructions = the question quoted in the paper's Methods ('A question was created by the authors asking "..."'). Response coding: no value labels exist on the Enjoy_* columns, so option_text is blank for both resp levels; 1 = option ticked, 0 = not ticked, established from the data: the raw 'Emjoy' string (comma-separated selected option numbers) equals the set of Enjoy_*==1 columns for 609 of 616 low/high-PWB respondents, and the Enjoy_* columns reproduce Table 3 counts in 45 of 46 cells exactly (the exception, Enjoy_09 high-PWB, is 25 in the data vs 27 printed, but the printed 7.8% = 25/321, so the printed n is the paper's typo). RESPONSE-DATA DEFECT: the source .sav only dummy-coded the Enjoy_* columns for the low (n=295) and high (n=321) well-being groups the paper analysed. 321 of the 322 middle-group respondents (Well_being_3groups=2) have Enjoy_*=0 on every item although their Emjoy string records exactly 5 selections each; one low-group respondent is also all-zero; the live table carries the same 322 all-zero ids (sum distribution 0:322, 2:1, 4:2, 5:612, 8:1; live per-item % identical to the .sav, e.g. Enjoy_01 28.6). Those zeros are not real non-selections. A further 7 low/high rows disagree with their Emjoy string. Fix belongs in the processing script (derive the 0/1 columns from Emjoy, or drop the middle group) -- not an item-text issue.
